notes.title: First Content Update for Seeds of Calamity!
notes.content:
[p]Hello! Today I’m here to announce the first official content update for Seeds of Calamity![/p][p] [/p][p][b]Introducing the Sky Pheasant and Wooly Boar![/b] Starting in Year 2, talk to Finn to purchase these new adorable farm animals. They can be housed in the existing pens but keep in mind that each pen can only hold 4 animals.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/bfaad514d59b94f9ff62e54b4d0d8ea80eda52eb.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Refine Wool and Fur with the Spinning Wheel![/b] You can now refine the wool you get from Snowtop Sheep and Wooly Boars to make it more valuable in the same way that Pickling Vessels work for Rock Hen Eggs (and now Sky Pheasant Eggs!).[/p][p]But how can you get your hands on this new device? Keep an eye on your mailbox! Once you have repaired the Ritual Stone on the farm and have purchased your first Snowtop Sheep, you will receive a letter from Yri who has an interesting book for you… [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/17683cd311481eb0f17226dceb28844b589500bf.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]New Egg, New Recipes![/b] With the new Sky Egg animal product, comes new cooking recipes! You can now purchase the Poached Eggs recipe during the Rock Hen Carnival. And after buying your first Sky Pheasant, Helena will want a word with you…[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/610d98aeb305a8e87a281ba99b289dccf3558e4c.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p][b]View Shrine Offerings from Anywhere![/b] You can now view all shrine offerings from your Journal menu in the Achievements section.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/9d9d029951495285c3801b209b2f0188308db8a6.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p][b]New Adorable Companion![/b] With this update I have also added a new companion type: Snowtop Sheep. You can change your companion at any time by using the mirror in your farmhouse. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/6d74deee99d62600a0e5573c093adb949739c669.png"][/img] [/p][p]Thank you for all your feedback and I hope you enjoy this new content. <3

With this update I also did a bunch of bug fixes and other minor feature changes:

[b]Game Play[/b]: [/p][list][*][p]You will now be able to interact with everything inside of the farmhouse while the internal storage is being upgraded.[/p][/*][*][p]The chest behind the waterfall south of the farm can now only be opened once.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a cutscnene with Jorund from being triggered too many times.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the shrine interior display for some players that only have 1 offering left to complete.[/p][/*][*][p]Placing fertilizer in the rain will maintain the watered state as expected when returning to your farm.[/p][/*][*][p]Smoothed a quest interaction with Lady Valeska when upgrading your Ritual Stone.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bugged fishing spot on Jorund's island.[/p][/*][/list][p] [b]Dungeon[/b]: [/p][list][*][p]Missing a fishing catch in the dungeon will no longer count towards the fishing spot. So now you can catch 3 fish at each spot even if you miss.[/p][/*][*][p]Using a pickaxe on tilled dirt no longer costs energy.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an exploit with the minecart treasure chest puzzle.[/p][/*][/list][p] [b]UI and Controller Support[/b]: [/p][list][*][p]Some players were able to buy Quality Hay before unlocking Coarse Hay. This has been fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]You will now no longer loose geodes when placing geodes from a different level in the same slot when breaking geodes at the crafting bench.[/p][/*][*][p]You will no longer lose a book if you turn in multiple books at once to the bookshelf in your farmhouse.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the cost of acorns and pinecones in the general store to 100 instead of 200 gold.[/p][/*][*][p]Added more spacing between characters for all hi definition fonts to increase readability, especially when entering animal names.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bad interaction with tree tappers and the animal pen when using tools with controller.[/p][/*][/list][p] [b]Crafting Changes[/b]: [/p][list][*][p]Reduced the Gold Bar recipe to use 1 less ore and 1 less Attuned Crystal, bringing it in line with the Iron Bar.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the Platinum Bar recipe to only need 1 Enhanced Crystal.[/p][/*][*][p]All Ritual Stone crafts should now craft much faster.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Talk to you soon,
Jenny[/p][p][/p][p]If you want to dive deeper into the development of this game and be the first to know about any exciting announcements, sign up for my mailing list here: [url="https://www.laboriouslarkstudios.com?utm_source=steam_event"]Sign up here![/url][/p]

notes.title: Patch Version 0.10.16.5
notes.content:
Hello! I've been working hard this past week to fix as many bugs as possible. I'll be putting out another bug fix patch soon but here is what is in today's patch.

Change log:

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
[list]
[*] Farming exp balance changes.
[*] The game will now default to the language of your Steam Client if the game has support for that language.
[*] The barrel to the right of the fireplace in the farmhouse has been removed. This was causing some items to get stuck after they had finished crafting.
[*] Fixed the seed prices in the general store from being calculated incorrectly after taking the seed price reduction perk.
[*] Updated the sprites for the outfit top when walking to no longer have missing pixels.
[*] I removed the option to buy the Light Chair and Table in the Midsummer Fair. This was a mistake on my part. You are supposed to buy these from Ingrid, the travelling merchant. If you have bought the recipe but don't see it in your crafting table, you can safely destroy the recipe item.
[*] The player should no longer get stuck after leaving chairs in the tavern.
[*] Opening and placing a small chest should be smoother now.
[*] You can no longer get infinite rewards from Garin after the Harvest Stew cutscene.
[*] Fixed festival decorations being visible in the evening if you missed the festival.
[*] Fixed the pickaxe animation playing on loop after completing a bounty.
[*] Fixed the Soil Samples in the quest "The Start of a Discovery" from not being accessible when using a controller.
[*] Some players were unable to play any of the festival mini games, this should now be fixed.
[/list]

[b]UI and Controller Support:[/b]
[list]
[*] The language menu control hint display will now behave as expected.
[*] Fixed the Return Crystal disappearing when sorting the inventory. I plan to add in the next patch a way for you to get back the Return Crystal if you have lost it.
[*] Prevented Lady Valeska's tool upgrade menu from showing after you have already upgraded every tool.
[*] Fixed a display issue when tabbing in the letter menu and Yri's shop with the controller.
[*] You can no longer open a small chest that has been broken. This is to prevent item loss when storing items in a chest that has been broken.
[*] Minor text changes.
[/list]


Thank you to everyone who has reported bugs and feedback. <3 


Talk to you soon,
Jenny

notes.title: Only 2 days left!
notes.content:
Today, I wanted to talk to you about my favorite feature to design, animate, write, and code in Seeds of Calamity.

I had a lot of fun designing the combat for this game. I’ve been so glad that the reception for the combat has been positive! It was a lot of work but I’m really happy with the results. Turn based combat is like a puzzle. I wanted each battle to be a new challenge for you to “solve”. I tried to make each enemy feel unique or at least present a new challenge. 

My favorite animations by far are the baby farm animals. They are just so cute and making all the unique idle animations for them was fun.

The fox spirits Rion and Tion are my favorite npcs to write. They play off of each other so well and I’ve enjoyed their funny dialog.

My favorite coding challenges were the festival mini games. It’s fun to code a game within a game. Making a small enclosed game loop was very satisfying and a nice change of pace from some of the larger features.

Tomorrow I will be back to give some insider tips and tricks to make your first few days in-game as smooth as possible.


Talk to you tomorrow,
Jenny

notes.title: Only 3 days left!
notes.content:
I can’t believe there's only 3 days left until the release of Seeds of Calamity. It’s been almost exactly 5 years since this game was just an idea in my head.

I’m a web developer for my day job and often had the passing thought that it would be cool to make a video game. When I decided to take the plunge and get serious about designing one of my own, I wanted to make a game similar to my favorite game: Stardew Valley. But I also wanted to draw inspiration from other games that I love such as Hades, Zelda, and Pokémon.

This entire adventure has been both the most creatively rewarding project I’ve ever taken on while also being the most challenging. Coding was familiar to me from the start, but I had never created a single piece of pixel art before starting this game! It took a lot of practice and iteration to get to the art you see in-game today. :)

This has been a labor of love and I truly mean it when I say “I hope you enjoy playing the game as much as I’ve enjoyed making it”. <3

Now that we are so close to the release, you will be hearing from me every day until launch. Tomorrow I'll be back to talk about my favorite features in the game.


Talk to you tomorrow,
Jenny

notes.title: Combat Spells Deep Dive
notes.content:
[b]Combat Spells Deep Dive[/b]
Today I want to dig deep into the combat for Seeds of Calamity. For those of you who don’t know, there is a three-level dungeon north of the village that you can explore. The dungeon has resources, puzzles, and dangerous creatures to fight. The battles are a turn based where you defeat your enemies by using elemental spells.

You will be able to buy spells in town from the former professor, Lady Valeska (for a price, of course). She sells spells from 3 different elements: Water, Air, and Fire. In the beginning of the game, you will only have access to Water spells but once you level up your combat skill, you will have access to the other elements.

So as not to spoil too much, I will only talk about the Water and Air elements today. Water spells can give your enemies a debuff that lowers their attack damage. This is especially useful when you need to wait a turn or two for your most powerful spells to be available. 

Air spells are a bit different. They can give enemies a debuff that makes them stunned and unable to attack for a turn but can also give you a buff that makes you much harder to hit. Air spells usually have shorter cooldowns and are better at single target attacks than multiple targets.

While sticking to just one element is viable, the more powerful spells use multiple elements. For example, a powerful Air spell will only have a chance to hit a target normally, but if that enemy has the Water debuff, that attack will always hit.

I highly encourage you to experiment and discover which elemental spell combinations are the most powerful.

notes.title: Skill Trees and Perks
notes.content:
[b]Skill Trees and Perks[/b]
Hello and a belated happy New Year!

In Seeds of Calamity, there are 5 different skills you can gain experience in. Farming, Fishing, and Cooking for your player character and Artifact Hunting and Combat for your companion. A skill can only be leveled up by sleeping at night.

At levels 3, 5, and 8 you will be able to select a permanent skill perk. These perks are quite powerful and let you customize how you play the game.

For example, when you reach level 3 farming, you will be able to pick between getting a skill perk that makes seeds cheaper or having a chance to get an extra animal product per day. Another example is when you reach combat level 5 you can pick between dealing more damage with single or multiple target spells.

notes.title: Treasure and Tools
notes.content:
[b]Treasure Maps[/b]
These are rare rewards from books, quests, or mountain treasure chests. Treasure maps can be viewed from your inventory. They each show an image of somewhere around the village with an X on it. If you find the place the map shows you, then you can interact with it to get a reward.

These rewards can be gems, crafting supplies, and other items well worth your time to find.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/96ca837bdd1d6871539a382d895de80928923170.png[/img]

[b]Tools[/b]
Tools are always accessible from the action bar at the bottom of your screen instead of in your inventory. My goal was to make it so you can’t “forget” your tools and can use them at any time.

You can also upgrade your tools by talking to Lady Valeska. Upgrading tools can increase the area of effect for your watering can, scythe, and hoe, allow you to gather resources deeper in the dungeon for your axe and pickaxe, and allow you to gather rare fish with your fishing pole. If you upgrade your scythe enough, you’ll be able to use it to harvest crops which makes harvesting much faster.

Tool upgrades while expensive, are well worth the investment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/0f7418872a2145604f1494e46f90adf57b7211be.png[/img]

notes.title: New Title and Major Demo Update!
notes.content:
[h2]New Title[/h2]
[b]Pine Lily Village will now be called [i]Seeds of Calamity[/i][/b]! This is still the game you’ve always known but the story has been much improved so the title has changed to reflect that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/2032178696cf3c4ab096333b54f59db8e5cb7575.png[/img]

[h2]Major Demo Update[/h2]
[b]Of course, with the new story comes a demo update! [/b]There is a new opening cutscene and more fleshed out villager backstories (and a ton of bug fixes). Because of how many changes I’ve made, unfortunately you will not be able to use an old save 

(sorry about that!)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/a524d0314f27f1f1e078db7c2410dc29b6db2612.png[/img]

[h2]What’s going on?![/h2]
So, you might be thinking: [i]“These changes are great and all but what gives? You announce a publisher partnership and then next thing I know you’re changing the title of the game! Seems sus.” [/i]

I assure you, all of the changes to the game have been designed and executed by me. I had actually been considering changing the story of the game before I even met with a publisher and longtime followers will know that I’ve changed the story of the game a few times already.[b] I’ve always loved the characters of the game but struggled with the world building.[/b]

[h3]So that’s what I’ve changed![/h3]
[b]Seeds of Calamity is a JRPG inspired world full of heroes and magic[/b]. During a great war between nations, an all-powerful beast called the [i]Great Calamity[/i] was summoned. It caused so much devastation, that the two waring nations agreed to a peace treaty. [b]That was 20 years ago and now you are tasked with helping rebuild from that war.[/b]

[b]You’ll send supplies back to the main city from your farm to help with the reconstruction efforts.[/b] Along the way, you’ll complete quests for the villagers, defeat dangerous creatures in the dungeon, and all other farming sim activities you’ve come to know and love.

[b]I hope you enjoy the new and improved demo.[/b] As always, if you have any feedback for the game, feel free to post on the Steam forum or fill out the survey from the main menu of the demo. I read every post and really appreciate it. 😊

Finally, [b]Seeds of Calamity[/b] will be participating in the [b]Cozy Quest[/b] festival between November 14-17th. So if you’re looking for other great cozy games, stay tuned for tomorrow!

notes.title: Diving into the Mountain!
notes.content:
There are three levels to the mountain and you will only be able to access lower levels after defeating the boss of the previous level. On your way to the boss, you’ll encounter many different encounters such as: 

[b]Gathering[/b]: You will be able to mine and fish for resources in the mountain and even encounter a treasure chest or two. Keep in mind that you will need to upgrade your tools to be able to use them in the lower levels.

[b]Puzzle[/b]: A mental challenge with a high reward chest at the end. Can be a nice break though, if you’re itching for a fight, you can decide to skip the reward and move on. 

[b]Combat[/b]: You will most likely encounter combat as you make your way to the boss of each level. Normal enemies are not too challenging but if you’re brave enough, you can take on Elite enemies. Win two fights with Elite enemies will unlock the ability to open a special treasure chest after defeating the boss.

[b]Teleport[/b]: If you think your pack is too full or your healing resources too light, you can always teleport back to the entrance of the mountain from the crystal teleport pools.

notes.title: Portrait Art Update
notes.content:
If you’ve played the beta versions of Pine Lily Village last year, you would have seen the old portrait art for the villagers. In my opinion, it was a bit lacking. I did my best but I wasn’t happy with what I could create on my own. 

So, I contacted an artist who agreed to remake all the portraits. She was great to work with and I’m super happy with what she created. The NPC portraits now have greater detail and a larger number of expressions which really brings them to life.

Here are a few of my favorites:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/2cb4a776016531a89c6e12cff5d517af4bc42605.png[/img]

Finn is the carpenter and rancher for Pine Lily village. He is very easy going and always happy to help out.

notes.title: Level Up!
notes.content:
There are 6 skills you can level up: Farming, Reading, Fishing, Ranching, Cooking, and Combat. You will gain experience in each skill by using them. For example, you gain experience in the Farming skill by, among other activities, planting and harvesting crops, and experience in the Combat skill by defeating enemies and unlocking new spells.

But what is the point of leveling up your skills? Well, as you can see below, at certain levels you gain a new passive effect or unlock for that skill. For example, at level 4 Farming, you will have an increased chance of harvesting higher level crops as well as unlocking the recipe for sprinklers which will automatically water your crops.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.content:
Here are some questions (with answers!) that I get asked frequently for your perusal. 

[b]Will you be able to romance/marry NPCs?[/b] Not right now. I want the characters of Pine Lily Village to be able to grow and have complex relationships with each other outside of the player. I’ll be able to develop the quest variety and writing far more because of this. 

[b]Will there be multiplayer/local co-op? [/b]I’m not planning on adding multiplayer at this time. If the game sells amazingly, I’ll consider it.

[b]How can you follow the development?[/b] The best way is to join my mailing list! I send more in-depth updates and will always update my mailing list of any exciting news (alpha testing, new trailer, etc.) before I post anywhere else. [url=https://www.laboriouslarkstudios.com?utm_source=steam_event]Sign up here![/url] You can also follow me on social media linked below.

[b]Will Pine Lily Village be coming to consoles?[/b] Potentially. I would love to put Pine Lily Village on consoles, especially the Switch but I would have to contract out the porting. So if the game sells well, then yes, for sure.

[b]Will there be post launch support/updates?[/b] Of course! I love working on this game and plan to continue supporting and updating it long after it launches.

notes.title: Planting and Harvesting Update

To start, you will need to buy seeds from the general store or, if you're lucky, find seasonal “mixed seeds”  when scything grass or chopping trees. Mixed seeds will grow a random crop from the current season.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41312751/089e714732c4db2cec6d3781d5e3604a42abb54c.png[/img]

Then you will need to hoe the ground, plant your seeds, and water them. Make sure you water your crops everyday or they won’t grow! If it rains, you can skip watering for that day.

Finally, after a set number of days, you will get to harvest the fruits of your labor!
